title: Keyproof acceptance playbook: SSO, RBAC, Audit Telemetry, and KMS/HSM evidence
creator: Elena Morales
description: Purpose: Provide a prescriptive, testable acceptance playbook (the 'Keyproof') for verifying SSO/SAML integration, RBAC configuration, audit telemetry capture/retention, and KMS/HSM key management artifacts prior to allowing a private/VPC deployment to pass the security gate. This ticket codifies required artifacts, deterministic verification steps, sign-off owners, and rollback criteria so Product, Security, and Ops can consistently evaluate readiness for customer onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Customer SAML 2.0 metadata uploaded and validated against our smoke harness with a successful SSO login from at least 2 IdP principals (okta/test-idp) in staging (evidence: idp-metadata.xml, smoke-harness log).

RBAC: Canonical RBAC matrix exists for the deployment showing role -> permission -> resource mappings; automated policy simulator run with 'least-privilege' test cases passing (evidence: rbac-matrix.csv, simulator-report.pdf).

Audit telemetry: Audit events for authentication, role changes, key operations, and admin actions are emitted to the configured audit store with schema-compliant fields and retention policy applied (1 year default). A 72-hour replay of synthetic events shows no gaps and indices are queryable (evidence: audit-tail-index.log, replay-report.json).

KMS/HSM integration: KMS envelope encryption validated end-to-end for application secrets and model keys. HSM signing test executed (if customer-selected HSM) with successful quorum sign and verify (evidence: kms-conn.txt, hsm-signature.log).

Key rotation and escrow: An automated key-rotation run completes without data loss in staging and escrow artifacts are recorded per policy. Rotation test must include rollback path verification (evidence: rotation-runbook.md, rotation-results.csv).

Operator controls: Console RBAC flows for granting/revoking admin access have audit entries and UI actions match backend events in the audit log (evidence: console-action-trace.png, audit-action-lines.log).
Security review: Threat modeling and architecture review completed with Security sign-off ticket linked and findings resolved or mitigated (evidence: sec-review-4512, mitigation-list.md).

Documentation: All required onboarding artifacts (SAML guide, RBAC mapping template, KMS/HSM runbooks, audit retention statement) are present in the customer evidence bundle and referenced by the sign-off checklist.
checklist: Collect SAML metadata from customer and run SSO smoke harness in staging (owner: Onboarding Eng)
Produce canonical RBAC matrix and run policy simulator (owner: Security PM)
Confirm audit pipeline endpoints and retention settings; perform 72-hour replay (owner: Observability Eng)
Execute KMS integration validation; if HSM selected, run signing/quorum test (owner: Crypto Eng)
Run key rotation + rollback simulation in staging, validate data decryptability post-rotation (owner: Platform Eng)
Consolidate evidence bundle (SAML metadata, RBAC matrix, replay report, KMS logs, runbooks) and upload to secure drive (owner: Product Manager)
Security team to review evidence bundle and log acceptance/concerns (owner: Security Engineering)
Legal to confirm export/compliance considerations for customer artifacts (owner: Legal)
Final sign-off by Product, Security, and Ops recorded in approvals section (owner: PM Lead)
If any critical failure, execute rollback runbook and block production onboarding until remediation verified (owner: Ops Lead)
decisions: Adopt SAML 2.0 metadata + fingerprint verification as the standard ingest format for all private deployments to simplify compatibility and auditing.
RBAC will be represented as a canonical CSV matrix for onboarding artifacts; runtime enforcement uses policy-engine v2 with the simulator used as acceptance test.
Default audit retention for private deployments is set to 365 days; customers may request different retention via contract but must provide justification and acceptance from Security.
KMS integration will be supported using our KMS abstraction; for HSMs we require a documented signing test and escrow manifest. HSM vendor-specific steps are captured in vendor runbooks.
Evidence bundle must include both human-readable runbooks and machine-verifiable logs to allow automated consumption by Security automation tools.
qa_plan: QA will run the SSO smoke harness across two IdP variants, run the policy simulator against the RBAC matrix, perform audit replay and search queries, validate KMS encrypt/decrypt across test artifacts, and run HSM signing verification if applicable. Evidence artifacts stored in secure drive and linked to ticket.
rollback_criteria: Any failed KMS rotation, loss of audit events for >1 hour, SSO authentication regressions affecting >5% of synthetic users, or RBAC escalations discovered during simulator runs must trigger immediate rollback according to the onboarding rollback runbook and block production onboarding until remediated.
notes: This playbook is intentionally prescriptive to reduce variability in security gate reviews. Next steps: integrate evidence bundle upload into the onboarding console, and automate as many simulator checks as possible (follow-up ENG ticket proposed). Consider adding a cryptographic attestation manifest to the evidence bundle for stronger non-repudiation.
